prerequisite: The drawing has a layer of edge polylines (0-ISLAND) and an existing-ground TIN surface with geometry (EG)
fixture_requirements: >= 2 polylines on the edge layer, at least one with an arc segment
At least one polyline entirely inside the surface (verifies off_surface == 0)
A fragment with < 3 vertices on the same layer (verifies min_length / handles can filter it out)
Another empty-shell surface in the drawing (design / Surface1) to verify that a wrong surface name throws
assertions: Read-only node: no Commit; drawing dbmod and file size are unchanged after the run
samples == sum of the polylines' vertices (with step=0 one per vertex; closed lines do not count the first point twice)
with step>0 samples grow clearly, z_min only falls and z_max only rises (refinement can only widen the range)
off_surface is the number of points outside the surface; they are excluded from the z_* statistics and never silently treated as 0
a line whose samples are all outside the surface has z_* all null and is named in warnings; no throw
z_median is the sorted median; with an even count it is the mean of the two middle values
area/length match LIST on that polyline in CAD (arcs by true arc length, not chord)
with include_open=false open lines are excluded; by default (true) they are included (division of labour with survey_dredge_regions)
with handles given as a whitelist only those are sampled; when neither layer nor handles is given, throw
with names given as {handle: name} the result id uses that name; others fall back to P01/P02 numbering
a surface name absent from the drawing throws and names it
when nothing matches, throw and echo the layer and whitelist size instead of returning an empty result
with export_excel=true two sheets are written, 'Summary' and 'Points', and both entries appear in excel_files
two runs with the same parameters give byte-identical results (read-only idempotence)

with interior_step>0 each closed line's interior_samples is approximately area/interior_step^2, within 5% per line; this is the litmus test for ring correctness -- on lines with arcs a broken ring drops it to 0
interior_step and step are independent: z_* is the edge-line measure, z_in_* the in-area measure; the 'existing elevation' of an island/parcel is z_in_mean
ring building and point-in-area must reuse DredgeBuildRing / GridPointInPolygon; no separate implementation in this node

observed: 32 edge lines, 2056 vertices sampled on the existing ground, off_surface == 0, elevations 2.08~9.702 m, 4 seconds
step=2 refined to 9283 points, elevations 1.844~9.939 m; the area-weighted mean differed by only 0.03 m (vertices 6.40 / refined 6.43)
per_polyline area matches, line by line, the area survey_dredge_regions reports for the same lines
I31 (handle D904) z range 6.82~7.54 (vertices) versus 6.811~7.868 from survey_dredge_regions (2 m resampling); after refinement it converges to 6.81~7.83
interior_step=2: 53075 grid points, off_surface 0; the point counts of the 32 lines match area/4 line by line

the in-area mean is systematically higher than the edge mean (area-weighted 6.93 versus 6.40) -- the islands are drawn around local high ground, so the edges naturally sit on the surrounding low ground
not_yet_covered: the off_surface > 0 branch (all 32 lines in this drawing are inside the surface)
the include_open=false branch (all 32 lines in this drawing are closed in the DWG)
